summary: The change adds ticket-authenticated WebSocket RPC. The control plane issues one-use tickets at /workspace/rpc/connect and proxies /workspace/rpc/socket. The workspace server gets a WorkspaceSockets owner that handles per-client replacement, a heartbeat deadline, and a lifetime cap, plus a local-development ticket flow at /rpc/connect. The durable tests pass, and I found no blocking logic defect in the gateway path. The coverage gate fails, though: 39 changed lines are uncovered, including the whole local-development ticket flow and several security-relevant rejection branches.

findings.body: No test covers the local-development socket flow. That flow is POST /rpc/connect (http.ts 225-258), then a ticketed upgrade on /rpc/socket (http.ts 317-318), backed by WorkspaceSockets.issueTicket/consumeTicket (WorkspaceSockets.ts 56-66, 79). Nothing checks that a renderer or CLI token can get a ticket, that the ticket opens a socket only once, that a second ticket for the same clientId supersedes the first pending ticket, that OPTIONS returns CORS headers only for configured origins, or that a bad clientId or a GET returns 400. This is new behavior and has no test. Add temp tests against serveHaloHttp directly.

No test covers the rejection path for a gateway-authenticated /rpc/socket upgrade that has no valid x-halo-client-id, no finite x-halo-session-expires, or an expired x-halo-session-expires (lines 348-349). This branch stops a holder of a gateway, renderer, or CLI token from opening an unbounded socket without identity. Add a temp test that sends a bearer-authorized upgrade with missing, malformed, and past-expiry headers and expects 401.

testRequests.target: packages/workspace-server/src/server/http.ts:224-258 and WorkspaceSockets.ts:56-66,79 — local /rpc/connect issues a ticket (renderer and CLI tokens); OPTIONS returns 204 with CORS only for an allowed origin; GET or a malformed x-halo-client-id returns 400; the ticket opens /rpc/socket once (http.ts:317-318) and a reused ticket is rejected; a second issueTicket for the same clientId invalidates the first pending ticket
testRequests.rationale: The local-development ticket path is entirely uncovered.

testRequests.target: packages/workspace-server/src/server/http.ts:340-349 — a bearer-authorized /rpc/socket upgrade with a missing or invalid client id, or a non-finite or past x-halo-session-expires, gets 401
testRequests.rationale: This security-relevant rejection branch is uncovered.

testRequests.target: apps/control-plane/src/workspace/proxy.ts:79-96 — /workspace/rpc/connect returns 400 for GET or a malformed client id, 401 when createWorkspaceSocketTicket returns undefined, and 500 when it returns an error (stub AuthService)

apps/control-plane/src/auth/AuthService.ts:292,312,326,339,356 — the error-wrapping branches, plus consumeWorkspaceSocketTicket returning undefined when the session behind the ticket was revoked or has expired between issue and upgrade
testRequests.rationale: Line 356 is a real authorization outcome (a revoked session must not open a socket), and the catch branches are uncovered.

testRequests.target: packages/workspace-server/src/server/WorkspaceSockets.ts:41,104-105,111-112,127 — the sweep drops expired tickets; a socket error terminates the connection; a ping is answered by terminating the socket when bufferedAmount exceeds 8 MiB; close() terminates open connections
testRequests.rationale: The lifecycle and backpressure branches of the new socket owner are uncovered.
